neal: quick heads-upran a microbench on host pre-parse after the kernel swap. tiny requests (<64 tokens) got slower.

neal: numbers (p50 local): total 13.2ms -> host_parse 7.1ms, kernel_dispatch 3.1ms, decode 3.0ms

priya: host_parse is huge for a 2-token request. breakdown?

neal: tokenization ~4.3ms, grpc/http2 framing & splice ~1.0ms, writev coalesce debounce ~1.8ms; added ~0.6ms for synchronous KV prefetch on hits

jack: any new copies from the runtime change?

neal: yes runtime now inserts a wide->narrow copy path when packing KV metadata for kernel X. our small-request fast-path still triggers full parse so we pay the copy cost.

maria: repro snippet?

neal: curl to canary: curl -sS -X POST https://canary.redwood/api/v1/gen -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"hi"}' and /internal/prof?pretty on node. perf shows host_parse 7.1ms [tokenize 4.3ms][frame 1.0ms][io 1.8ms]

priya: proposals: stream tokenization output directly into send buffer for tiny requests, make KV prefetch best-effort async, early writev coalescing, and prefer kernel Y for <64 tokens to avoid wide->narrow copy.

jack: alternative: increase minibatch window for kernel X so host can coalesce small requests before packing. risk is slightly higher latency under low load.

maria: I'll run canary with async kvcache prefetch + earlier writev coalesce. jack add runtime flag for kernel preference and bump minibatch_ms=6 for canary.

neal: estimated win if canary succeeds: host_parse p50 7.1ms -> ~4.0ms, end-to-end p50 ~13.2ms -> ~10.1ms

priya: run load tests to ensure throughput not harmed. we need tokenization timings, kvcache hit/miss telemetry and tail latency.
